column7: 2026-11-02: parseBytes supports only plain numbers/B and binary units (KiB..YiB), case-sensitive. SI units (kB/MB/GB...) intentionally left out until the user checks with the storage team how to read them.

2026-11-02: Storage team answer: units without the 'i' (KB/kB, MB, GB...) are powers of 1024 on this branch (1 KB = 1024, 1 MB = 1048576), because users paste sizes from Windows Explorer. To be added to parseBytes in a later session; not part of the first commit.

2026-11-02: Billing (billing-svc) quotes in strict SI: when SI units (kB, MB, GB...) are added to parseBytes here, 1 MB must be exactly 1,000,000 bytes (powers of 1000), matching prettyBytes output. This differs from storage-app, where KB/MB/GB are powers of 1024. Until then SI units stay rejected.
